user.title: Connect to Paxton10
user.description: Choose how Home Assistant reaches the Paxton10 server.

data_description.route: Direct connects to the server on the site network. It's faster. Remote goes through Paxton's remote access service and works from anywhere.

data_description.target: The server's IP address or host name, for example 192.0.2.10. Home Assistant must be able to reach it on port 443.
data_description.username: The email address of the Paxton10 account. Use a dedicated account, so the Paxton event log shows what Home Assistant did.
data_description.password: Home Assistant stores only the password hash that the Paxton10 server expects.

data_description.target: The ID from the site's remote access address, for example abc123 from abc123.paxton10remote.com. You can paste the whole address.
data_description.username: The email address of the Paxton10 account. Use a dedicated account, so the Paxton event log shows what Home Assistant did.

error.invalid_auth: The username or password is wrong.
error.cannot_connect: Can't connect to the Paxton10 server: {error}
error.invalid_direct_target: Enter the server's IP address or host name.
error.invalid_remote_target: Enter the remote ID, for example abc123.
error.unknown: Unexpected error. Check the Home Assistant log.

abort.already_configured: This Paxton10 site is already set up.
abort.wrong_site: That server is a different Paxton10 site.

data_description.allow_door_control: Adds an Open button for each door and the gate. When off, Home Assistant sends no writes at all.
data_description.device_interval: How often to read the system summary and door lock state. A change in the offline device or alarm counts triggers a full device refresh.
data_description.device_full_interval: How often to read the full controller and entry panel list (firmware, battery, and status details) when nothing has changed. It's also read straight away when the offline device or alarm counts change, or a controller reports a hardware event. Minimum 60 seconds.
data_description.event_interval: Events arrive live from the server. This is how often to read the event log while the live connection is down. Minimum 5 seconds.
data_description.fallback: If the configured route fails, try the other one ({other_route}).
data_description.fallback_target: The address or remote ID for the {other_route} route. You can paste a whole address.
data_description.include_user_names: Adds user names to door events. Names are personal data, so this is off by default.
data_description.include_credential_names: Adds the name each credential was given in Paxton to access events, as it was entered.

error.fallback_target_required: Enter the fallback address or remote ID.

invalid_auth.message: The Paxton10 server rejected the stored credentials.

cannot_connect.message: Can't connect to the Paxton10 server: {error}

door_gone.message: This door is no longer on the Paxton10 server.

door_control_off.message: Door control is off in the Paxton10 options.

door_forbidden.message: The Paxton account isn't allowed to open {door}.

using_fallback_route.title: Paxton10 is using the fallback route
using_fallback_route.description: The configured {primary} route failed, so Home Assistant is connected over {active}. Check the network path to the Paxton10 server. This message clears when the {primary} route works again.
